summary: Specialize EventEmitter.on('data') because adding a data listener can change Readable flow state.

target.notes: Register via NodeEvents semantics and, if the stream has not been explicitly paused/readable-driven, switch it to flowing mode so chunks are delivered as data events.

semantics.flow_transition: null to true unless explicitly paused/readable listener rules prevent it
semantics.delivery: chunks emitted as data become consumed

caveats: A generic EventEmitter.on lowering is insufficient because it would miss the Readable state transition.
Mixing data/readable/pipe/async-iterator consumption styles can produce unintuitive behavior and remains runtime-managed.

tests.name: data listener starts flowing
tests.expected_behavior: readableFlowing becomes true as consumption starts

tests.name: explicitly paused stream stays paused until resumed
tests.input: const {PassThrough}=require('node:stream'); const r=new PassThrough(); r.pause(); r.on('data',()=>console.log('data')); r.write('x'); console.log(r.readableFlowing);
tests.expected_behavior: no data event before resume; readableFlowing remains false
